function: Transformer predicts each STA's future partial CSI (beamforming matrix) from historical feedback, so the AP updates precoders between sounding rounds in time-varying Wi-Fi MU-MIMO (pp. 7-9).
system: Downlink MU-MIMO, AP with 16 TX antennas, 8 STAs with 2 RX antennas each (2 streams), no RIS; 5.25 GHz, 20 MHz (242 tones), IEEE 802.11be (p. 9).
method: Encoder-decoder Transformer (4+4 layers, 8 heads) trained supervised with MSE on beamforming-matrix time series, plus spline interpolation; model-driven search sets the sounding period (pp. 7-10).
data_channel: IEEE TGbe channel model D (802.11be) in a MATLAB WLAN Toolbox link-level simulator with AR(1) time variation; 100,000 training and 10,000 test beamforming samples; no measurements (pp. 3, 9-10).
test_conditions: Same TGbe model D simulator for training (100,000 samples) and testing (10,000), 10 Hz Doppler; throughput at initial SINR 4-28 dB; no other channel model or Doppler (pp. 9-11).
baselines: Non-learned: vanilla EHT sounding with outdated partial CSI, fixed 20 ms sounding period; learned: LSTM, GRU and MLP predictors of similar size (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Prediction MSE (training and validation loss), instantaneous and average throughput (Mbps), optimal sounding period, CSI overhead reduction (pp. 10-11).
complexity: Transformer time complexity O(N_RF^2 N_ss^2)+O(G N_RF N_ss)+O(G N_RF); model size 8 Mbits; inference under 1 ms on a TPU; sounding-period search O(log2 n) or O(n) (pp. 7, 9, 10).
q1_support: p. 3: "shall adopt the IEEE TGbe channel model A-F"; p. 9: "the IEEE TGbe channel model D dataset" and "MATLAB IEEE 802.11be WLAN Toolbox with TGbe channel conditions". Standardized IEEE 802.11 model, not 3GPP.
q2_support: p. 10: "training samples and 10, 000 test samples" from the same simulator, with only TGbe model D (p. 9). Missing: no new channel model, Doppler, array or site; p. 12 leaves "partial CSI prediction with high Doppler speed" to future work.
q3_support: p. 10: "Transformer with the lowest training loss and validation loss stands out" against LSTM, GRU and MLP; p. 1: "baseline EHT sounding protocol that always uses outdated partial CSI", with "increasing the average throughput by up to 30.9%".
q4_support: p. 9: "The time complexity of the Transformer [36] can be written" as O(N_RF^2 N_ss^2)+O(G N_RF N_ss)+O(G N_RF); p. 10: "The inference time on our Tv5e TPU machine is less than 1 ms".
q5_support: p. 9: "The link-level simulator was developed with the aid of the MATLAB IEEE 802.11be WLAN Toolbox"; p. 10: "obtained from 11be link- level simulator". Missing: the data are generated in-house and no code, dataset link or release statement appears.
notes: q1 rests on the IEEE 802.11 TGbe channel model D, a standardized WLAN model outside the listed 3GPP set, for the reviewer to confirm; the time variation is the paper's own AR(1) model on the TGbe initial channel (p. 3). Area 2 because the learned part predicts partial CSI and is scored by MSE against LSTM, GRU and MLP (pp. 7, 10); the sounding-period search (Algorithm 1, p. 7) is model-driven and not learned. q3: the learned baselines are compared on prediction MSE only (p. 10), and the throughput comparison is against outdated CSI (p. 1).
